# site — the lets-dsa notebook

A static dashboard over the learning data: every solved problem, its signal, intuition,
pseudocode, code, defects and notes, plus pattern briefs, recall flashcards and a printable
cheat sheet. Search, light/dark mode, and it works on a phone.

**Nothing here is generated by a model.** `scripts/build-data.ts` parses the markdown
mechanically, writes JSON, and Vite builds a ~23 kB (gzipped) Preact app that reads that JSON.

```
questions/**/*.md ─┐
patterns/*.md      │   build-data.ts                         Vite
topics/*.md        ├─► gray-matter + remark (mdast) ─► public/data/*.json ─► dist/
config/*.json      │   split on "## ", map by config,
state/stats.json  ─┘   render markdown + Shiki at build time
```

## Commands

Run from `site/`.

| | |
|---|---|
| `npm install` | once |
| `npm run dev` | rebuild data, start dev server |
| `npm run build` | data + type-check + production build into `dist/` |
| `npm run build:public` | same, with private sections stripped (see below) |
| `npm run data` | just the JSON — prints a warning for every heading it could not map |

## Config, not code

| File | Decides |
|---|---|
| `config/content.config.json` | How each `## Heading` in a question file maps to a field (regex `match`), how it renders (`prose`, `table`, `pre`, `code`), when recall mode reveals it (`recall`), and whether it is `private`. Also the pattern-brief section map. |
| `config/site.config.json` | Where the data lives (`source`), the nav, overview widget order, problem-page section and meta order, pattern-page section order, readiness thresholds, band labels. |

When the question-file format drifts, `npm run data` lists the unmapped headings. Add a
rule to `content.config.json`; the parser itself should not need to change. Unmapped
sections are still rendered, under their own heading, so nothing is silently dropped.

## Data never enters git

`public/data/` and `dist/` are gitignored here, and listed in `.githooks/personal-paths`
at the repo root, so the hooks block them on the public branch too. The site's *code*
is framework and public; the *data* exists only where `questions/**` does.

## Deploying

`.github/workflows/site.yml` (at the repo root) builds and publishes to GitHub Pages on every
push to `main` that touches the data or the site. It only runs in `shubhamcodess/lets-dsa-sp`,
or in a repo with the Actions variable `DSA_SITE_ENABLED=true`. On the public framework repo
it is skipped.

One-time setup in the private repo: **Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions.**

Be aware:
- GitHub Pages from a **private** repo needs a paid plan (Pro, Team or Enterprise).
- Even then, a Pages site is **publicly reachable** by anyone with the URL. The page sends
  `noindex` and `robots.txt` disallows everything, but that only keeps it out of search,
  not away from someone who has the link. For a truly private dashboard, host the same
  `dist/` behind an auth layer such as Cloudflare Pages with Access.
- Set the repo variable `SITE_MODE=public` to publish the stripped edition instead.

## Public edition

`SITE_MODE=public` drops every section marked `"private": true` (defects, revisit log,
session log), the frontmatter keys in `publicStripFrontmatter`, submission URLs, company
tags, wrong first guesses, and the error profile. What stays is the reasoning: problem,
signal, intuition, ladder, pseudocode, code, complexity and notes.

## Moving this folder to its own repo

Everything `site/` needs is inside `site/`. To split it out:

1. Copy `site/` to the root of a new repo.
2. Copy `deploy/standalone-pages.yml` to `.github/workflows/pages.yml` there.
3. Set the variable `DATA_REPO` (e.g. `shubhamcodess/lets-dsa-sp`) and the secret
   `DATA_REPO_TOKEN` (a fine-grained token with read-only Contents on that repo).

The workflow checks out the data repo into `.data/` and sets `DSA_ROOT` to it. Locally,
do the same: `DSA_ROOT=/path/to/lets-dsa npm run dev`.

## Design

Paper and ink, one oxblood accent. Newsreader (variable, optical sizes) for display and
prose, IBM Plex Sans for interface, IBM Plex Mono for code. Fonts are self-hosted, Latin
only, woff2 only. No analytics, no external requests. All colours are tokens in
`src/styles/tokens.css`. Re-theme there.

| Path | |
|---|---|
| `src/views/` | one file per page: Overview, Problems, Problem, Patterns, Revise, Sheet, Foundations |
| `src/components/` | Shell, search palette, readiness ruler, heatmap, small typographic atoms |
| `src/lib/` | data loading, hash router, search (MiniSearch, loaded on first use), dates, theme |

Hash routing (`#/p/two-sum`) keeps the build host-agnostic. It works at any base path with
no server rewrites.
